classification.difficultyReason: Read the supplied central percentages and use symmetry to halve regions or remaining tails, then complement a tail for one-sided percentages. Earlier entries scaffold the hardest calculation; the repeated regions and decimal percentages add no new reasoning.

content.prompt: Use the graphs to answer these questions.

inlines.text: What percentage of scores have a z-score:

spec.description: Normal curve with central green region from −1 to 1, dashed bounds and centre, labelled central percentage and equal halves.
spec.mathematics: Standard normal symmetry; approximately 68% between −1 and 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph, including percentage annotations.

answer.worked: The graph gives 68% between −1 and 1. By symmetry, each half of this region is $68\%\div2=34\%$, and each side of 0 contains 50%. Each outer tail is $(100\%-68\%)\div2=16\%$. The percentage greater than −1 is $100\%-16\%=84\%$. Thus, in row order: 68%, 34%; 34%, 50%; 50%, 16%; 16%, 84%.

inlines.text: What percentage of scores have a z-score:

spec.description: Normal curve with central green region from −2 to 2, dashed bounds and centre, labelled central percentage and equal halves.
spec.mathematics: Standard normal symmetry; approximately 95% between −2 and 2.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph, including percentage annotations.

answer.worked: The graph gives 95% between −2 and 2. Each half of this region is $95\%\div2=47.5\%$. Each outer tail is $(100\%-95\%)\div2=2.5\%$. The percentage greater than −2, or less than 2, is $100\%-2.5\%=97.5\%$. Thus, in row order: 95%, 47.5%; 47.5%, 2.5%; 2.5%, 97.5%; 97.5%.

inlines.text: What percentage of scores have a z-score:

spec.description: Normal curve with central green region from −3 to 3, dashed centre, labelled central percentage and equal halves.
spec.mathematics: Standard normal symmetry; approximately 99.7% between −3 and 3.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph, including percentage annotations.

answer.worked: The graph gives 99.7% between −3 and 3. Each half of this region is $99.7\%\div2=49.85\%$. Each outer tail is $(100\%-99.7\%)\div2=0.15\%$. The percentage greater than −3, or less than 3, is $100\%-0.15\%=99.85\%$. Thus, in row order: 99.7%, 49.85%; 49.85%, 0.15%; 0.15%, 99.85%; 99.85%.
